title: Reconstruct InstructGPT
summary: Trace supervised instruction tuning, preference modeling, and PPO optimization, then implement both alignment objectives.

parts.title: Why supervised fine-tuning first?
parts.prompt: Why not train the policy directly from preference rewards starting from the base language model?
parts.answer: Demonstrations first place the policy in the region of helpful instruction-following behavior. Preference optimization can then refine responses instead of searching an enormous action space from scratch.
hints: The reward model is reliable only near its data.
SFT supplies a strong initial policy.

parts.title: Learning a reward model
parts.prompt: How do ranked response pairs become a scalar reward function?
parts.answer: A reward model scores each response. A Bradley-Terry style loss increases the chosen score relative to the rejected score, learning a ranking-compatible scalar signal.

parts.title: Why constrain PPO?
parts.prompt: Why include clipping and a KL penalty to the supervised policy?
parts.answer: The learned reward is imperfect and exploitable. Clipping and KL regularization limit policy movement, keeping outputs near human-written behavior and the reward model training distribution.
hints: The reference model acts as an anchor.

parts.title: Implement pairwise reward loss
parts.prompt: Compute the logistic loss that prefers a chosen response score over a rejected score.

parts.title: Implement PPO clipping
parts.prompt: Compute the elementwise minimum of unclipped and clipped probability-ratio objectives.
